A

Austin

Beware, these are not 8.5"x11" pieces of paper

Beware, these are not full sized pieces of paper like what you would pull out of a printer. If you plan to staple these to printed paper it can be quite annoying. They are significantly smaller. The pages also rip easily if you are not careful. They feel cheap and thin. Of course these notebooks ARE cheap, so you get what you pay for. I recommend the Five-Star gridline notebooks for higher quality and a full sized piece of paper.

M

Melaina Lara

Notes a notebook

These are decent quality and a great price. For some reasfinding graph notebooks isn't as easy as running into your nearest target where lined notebooks abound.Enter this 8 pack, I received 2 each of four colors and the quality was consistent and good for all of them. The pages are not thin, and I don't see a lot of bleed through. The graph printing is not too light or dark, and it's just what I would expect from a spiral notebook. The pages are perforated and tear out easily and cleanly.My two older kids use them for math class, and this 'bulk' set keeps me happy, since I have spares ready to go.

K

Kenny T.

Dark grid lines make it hard to read notes in pencil!

I really wish I hadn't bought the pack and only bought 1 notebook to try out. Next time I'm following my intuition. The blue lines for the grid are too darkly colored so that I don't want to write in pencil in my notebook because the dark grid lines make it hard to read. So now I use ink, and since ink bleeds through often, making it even harder to read my notes, I only use one sides of pages instead of 2. Not buying this again. Maybe it works for others but next time, make sure to include a picture of the inside!

#### Would recommend to all my fellow scribblers out there!

I never thought I'd be the kind of person to get excited about a notebook, but here I am, swooning over this wide-ruled one-subject wonder! It's like the reliable best friend who shows up on time, comes with the right color to your wedding, listens to your thoughts, and never judges your handwriting (no matter how messy). For the price, I was expecting a flimsy, fall-apart-at-the-seams kind of deal, you know the ones that get all tangled in the springs and you have to rip the page out, but nope! This notebook is sturdy, the pages are smooth, and the wide-ruled lines are like a warm hug for my sloppy writing. It's not fancy, but who needs fancy when you get the job done? This notebook is like the trusty sidekick that keeps your thoughts organized and your creativity flowing. And let's be real, it's not like I'm writing the next great American novel in here... but if I was, this notebook would totally be up to the task. In short, it's a great notebook for the price. No frills, no fuss, just good old-fashioned note-taking bliss. Five stars, would recommend to all my fellow scribblers out there!

# Mead Spiral Notebooks, 1 Subject, College Ruled, 70 Sheets, Assorted Colors, Color Selected For You May Vary, 1 Count (05512)
Brand: Mead
Category: Notebooks & Writing Pads > Spiral Notebooks

## Features
Perfect to use for 1 subject, this spiral notebook comes in handy for your favorite class or any project; With 70 college ruled, double-sided sheets, there’s plenty of notetaking space. Pages are perforated so they easily tear out with clean edges.; Notebook is 3-hole punched for storage in your favorite binder. This allows you to keep all your work organized and in one place.; Spiral binding will not snag and resists uncoiling to keep your notes together. Notebook covers are coated for durability.; Sheets measure 10-1/2" x 7-1/2" when torn out. Overall size of 10-1/2" x 8". Available in assorted colors: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Black.; NOTE: COLOR CHOICE IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR THIS ITEM, COLOR SHIPPED TO YOU IS SELECTED AT RANDOM, AND WILL VARY

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 2.22 USD.
Rated 4.3 from 538 reviews.
Top review: Great note book for the price cant beat 2 bucksThis notebook is standard issue fare,I just saw the same one for 50 cents on sale at a brick and mortar store. But quality wise, it's fine. The cover isn''t super stiff but protective enough and the pages are are fine. Lines straight and easy to see. Same notebook I have been using for decades. I do think the price a bit high for a 70 page notebook with no perforations on the pages but I opted to pay it so I can't rate lower because of it. It is the notebook I have used all of my life. This one is college ruled. I bought a wide ruled one as well. Both fine for what they are. I prefer perforated pages though so I don't have to rip pages out and have a bunch of broken holes and junk on the sides.This purchase is such a no brainer. Note that Amazon only lets you buy one with each order, but it can help you make the $25 free shipping threshold. At present, these are going for 48 cents versus the 51 cents I paid. You cannot purchase these in the grocery store for that price, which is where I usually get them. I go through these notebooks regularly, using them for shopping lists and planning events. Okay, I'm getting to the point that at times I have to write things down because I can't remember them otherwise. You say, why not post its? Yes, I use those too, but occasionally the project is much more than a post it can handle. For instance, when I go away for one or two weeks, there are a number of things I have to remember to do during the seven days before I leave. So, I dedicate a page for each day and write down the things that have to be done. Similarly, Thanksgiving is coming up. For the two weeks prior, I have a ton of things that need to be done before T Day, and then each day I check off the things as they are completed. Never mind Christmas. You get the idea. I don't care about whether there is a particular quality to the paper or whether the perforation is perfect. The pages are torn out as tasks are completed. And yes, I have even given them to my grandkids for their school projects, with no complaints.This isn’t a Mead “Five Star” notebook; it must be one of their cheaper bargain lines. I need a notebook that has a hard enough back cover that I can write on it without the support of a desk or a clipboard. It’s like they used the kind of cardboard on the back cover that they use for cereal boxes lately. Cheap. If you are going to use it only on a table or desk or clipboard, then it would probably work for you, but not if you plan on using it independently of any support.Also, why is it next to impossible to find *narrow* ruled (not college-ruled) notebooks? Hello paper product companies?Let me just say that if this notebook had any actual flaws, e.g. the paper gets stuck on the spiral ring (literally the worst problem I can think of when it comes to notebooks) or if some pages were blank, then I would not be so quick to dismiss the snooty notebook connoisseurs who rag on this item.There is not a single complaint any normal, sane person could make about these notebooks. They are the cheapest you can find and just as functional as any other bound grouping of lined papers. Yes, it is a bit floppy. Yes, the pages are thin enough that the next page will have faint and barely-noticeable pressure marks from your pen or pencil. Yes, your first-world sensitivities will be offended by all this. Who cares? It's $1 and the main market consists of starving college students who subsist on ramen that costs less than your typical notebook. Buying this notebook for cheap allows us to invest 300% more in ramen.My girls are headed back to school. They needed quite a few spirals to help them. I wanted something that was not to costly but at the same time not all the same color. These spirals did the trick.They are made from a average quality paper with a nice sturdy spiral. They come in great colors allowing my girls to have a different one for each subject. Since my girls are still young, these will be perfect and get the job done.I would also recommended them for college. They are perfect for a math class or anything that will be short term use.Overall if you still are in school or have kids, these are amazing. They will get the job done.what I was looking for. They are as described but not pictured. The ones I received have the SFI Certified Sourcing leaf design, which were incidentally the ones I was hoping to receive, so it's all to the good. Non-perforated, so good for those who don't need or want the paper to come out. The paper is nice, but not premium, obviously, and it comes from a third-party certified responsible and renewable source. Great value, great price, good for our world. Btw, I ordered 5 and got the colors: green, red, yellow, purple, and the lighter blue.Edit: I forgot to mention that they arrived pretty fast; 3 or 4 days.2nd Edit: when I bought these they were pretty cheap; around 1-2 dollars each. Also, maybe you should read the details closer next time you buy something online. The description clearly says it's one per order and lists the available colors. Be savvy.Got it out of the box and the spirals are all squished flat so I cannot even open the notebook all the way. Usually I would just to to the store but I figured I was ordering other things might as well order that too, not doing that again.No happy at all 7 pound for 1 book, I would like a refund!!!WOW. I was under the impression I was getting at least 6 notebooks not just 1. So Frgn mad 😡. Why the he’ll would anyone want to spend over 8$ for one notebook with only 70 pages. RIP OFF. Booooooooo🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬Buyer beware! This item is ONE NOTEBOOK, not a package if 6 add states in the manufacturer's description.Save your money and buy from WalMart.Un cuaderno de calidad básica
